newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Canadian troops to visit Zaire daily.
newsitem.headline: Canadian troops to visit Zaire daily.

text.p: The multinational force for central Africa has deployed four Canadians in the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi with a mandate to cross daily into Zaire and help the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR track refugees.
"We are here to assist UNHCR in any way we can," the head of the four-man team, Major Ron Puddister of the Royal Canadian Dragoons, told Reuters in eastern Zaire on Wednesday.
Canada offered last month to lead a multinational force charged with assisting Rwandan Hutu refugees missing in Zaire.

The Canadian commander, Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril, has set up his headquarters in the Ugandan capital Kampala but the force has not started work because of opposition from Zaire, Rwanda and the Zairean rebels who hold much of eastern Zaire.

Puddister, who was part of a 17-man Canadian liaison team based in the Rwandan capital Kigali, said the main task of the Gisenyi four was to gather information for a possible larger deployment on the ground by talking to humanitarian agencies.

"General Baril returns to New York on Friday and U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien is going to be briefing the United Nations. While we wait for a decision here we are going to be based in Gisenyi coming over to Goma each day, helping UNHCR in whatever way we can," he said.

Despite weeks of aerial reconnaissance and a pile of anecdotal evidence from the field, no one yet has a clear picture of what has happened to hundreds of thousands of Rwandans missing since the rebels took over in October.
"Our major problem with the refugees is that those people out there (the aid agencies in eastern Zaire) are not sure of their status, they don't know what to do or where to go.

"UNHCR say that refugees are gathered in the Lowa river valley northeast of Walikale but humanitarian agencies and the Banyamulenge rebels will not go into the area because of security," Puddister said.
Aid agencies also say there is a large group of refugees to the southwest of Beni, 250 km (160 miles) north of Goma, but journalists who went to the area found no trace of them.
